content.text: King is a compendium card game played in many countries including Belgium, Italy, Portugal, Russia, Turkey, Colombia, and Brazil. Despite its English name, there is no evidence it was ever played in English-speaking countries. The game consists of a series of rounds with different objectivesâ€”some negative (avoiding specific cards or tricks) and some positive (winning tricks). It is closely related to Barbu, Kierki, and Trex.

The game is known by the English name 'King' in many non-English speaking countries, leading to speculation about English origins. However, no evidence exists of it being played in English-speaking countries. It likely evolved from European compendium games in the early 20th century.
4 players playing individually (partnerships form in some variants).
Standard 52-card deck. Aces are generally high.
Each player receives 13 cards. The dealer rotates clockwise.
